newsitem.title: UK: Japan tops govt bond league in bleak week -Salomon.
newsitem.headline: Japan tops govt bond league in bleak week -Salomon.

text.p: Japanese government bonds were top of the pops -- but only in local currency terms -- in a generally bleak week for government bond returns, according to Salomon Brothers data issued on Friday.
JGBs achieved returns of 0.33 percent in yen in the week ended Thursday, helped by Tokyo stock falls.
In dollar terms, Japanese bond returns were at the other extreme, finishing bottom of the World Government Bond Index at minus 1.48 percent, hit by yen weakness early in the week.
In local currency terms, only three other countries managed positive returns, with the dollar bloc scraping ahead of anything Europe could offer.
Canada and the United States came second and third on the list with returns of 0.07 percent and 0.06 percent respectively.
Austria managed 0.02 percent, while Germany was fifth but in negative territory at minus 0.03 percent.

British gilts finished bottom of the pack in local terms at minus 0.61 percent, pulled down by publication of December monetary minutes showing Bank of England governor Eddie George warned that a half-point base rate rise might be needed early this year.

European high yielders also turned in an unimpressive performance during the week. Sweden and Italy, giving negative returns of 0.53 percent and 0.45 percent respectively, were next to Britain at the foot of the league table.
Fellow high-yielder Spain turned in a slightly better performance, halfway down the table at minus 0.13 percent.
France was just below there on minus 0.16 percent.
In dollar terms, the week's results were even worse, with only the United States giving positive returns.
Austria was runner-up with returns of minus 0.03 percent, followed by Germany (minus 0.06 percent) and Finland (minus 0.09 percent).
Next to Japan at the foot of this table was Britain on minus 1.43 percent, then Italy on minus 0.99 percent.
The bond index as a whole was down 0.03 percent in local currency terms and down 0.50 percent in dollar terms.

Salomon's bond index is calculated using all government bonds with over one year to maturity, weighted for market capitalisation. Only bonds freely available to institutional investors and with a certain minimum amount outstanding are included. Returns take account of price moves and accrued interest.
